messages:
maria: starting a small FP8 canary for jl-13b-awq on L40S pool (region-us-west). rolling to 5 hosts. seeing weird intermittent �nan� in attention GEMM after ~2k tokens in some sessions. not consistent across chairs. posting trimmed logs below.

kevin: thanks — can you paste the tiny log snippet? also is this only on L40S or H100 too?

maria: only L40S so far, H100 canary looks clean. snippet:
```
[2025-03-14T15:02:12Z] kernel_fp8_gemm: produced nan at tile (23,0)
[2025-03-14T15:02:12Z] kv_cache: extend request 4096 -> 6144 tokens
[2025-03-14T15:02:12Z] allocator: failed to allocate 64MB from chunk_pool, fragmentation=0.78
[2025-03-14T15:02:12Z] runtime: falling back to fp16_gemm (fallback_reason=alloc_pressure)
```

maria: quality delta shows spike in log-perplexity for affected sessions (~6% after fallback).

anya: hmm looks like an allocator fragmentation -> fallback chain. L40S allocator uses many small chunks and our FP8 kernels expect tightly packed tiles. when fallback to fp16 we get numeric drift + different packing -> perf/quality change.

raj: also check tile alignment. our FP8 fused kernels assume aligned stride to 256 bytes for KV buffers; if allocator returns unaligned slices after repeated extend/free cycles we get partial tiles that trigger fallback paths. I've seen a similar cliff with long prefixes.

kevin: can we reproduce locally with stress harness? create 50 sessions with gradually increasing prefix length to force multiple KV reallocations. I can instrument allocator stats (coalesces, free runs).

maria: running a repro now. quick telemetry from first run:
```
sessions:50
avg_prefix_when_fail: 4120
allocator.coalesce_runs: 3
allocator.max_fragment: 0.81
fallback_rate: 0.04
perplexity_delta_when_fallback: +5.8%
```

infra-bot: canary-deploy 1749123456: started (hosts=5). metrics: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/canary/1749123456

anya: mitigation ideas:
- pre-reserve a small scratch pool at model load (512MB) to satisfy KV expansions so allocator doesn't chop up the large HBM quickly
- set runtime env REDWOOD_FP8_ALIGN=256 (align KV allocations)
- try kernel flag force_pad_tile=true which pads KV tile to alignment boundary instead of creating partial tile fallback

raj: additional low-risk patch: when prefix>4096 set kv_chunk_size=128MB instead of 32MB. that reduces fragmentation by giving larger contiguous run. downside is slightly higher steady-state HBM usage.

kevin: we should also add an observability guard: when fallback_rate > 0.5% over 5m for FP8 -> auto-turn-off and instrument a reduced rollout. avoid noisy regressions in prod.

maria: I pushed a small canary with REDWOOD_FP8_ALIGN=256 + pre-reserve=256MB to two hosts. initial results: fallback_rate down to 0.002, no nan seen so far (10m). perf hit minimal. will run longer.

deploy-bot: rolled canary patch to host group l40s-smallpool (2/5) — config: REDWOOD_FP8_ALIGN=256 pre_reserve_kv_mb=256

anya: note on numeric drift: when fallback happens mid-session, we re-run later tokens with different kernel paths which leads to divergent logits. for deterministic rolling you might want to prefer consistency: if fallback happened once for a session, continue with fallback (i.e., disable FP8 for that session) to avoid inconsistent user-visible deltas.

raj: agreed. add a session-level flag: session.runtime.force_precision=fallback_precision. and a short TTL so it resets cleanly.

maria: action items:
- kevin: run scaled repro (50->500 sessions) + collect allocator traces (ETA 3h)
- anya: prototype pre-reserve + force_pad_tile change in runtime (ETA 1d)
- raj: add session-level fallback consistency TTL (ETA 1d)
- infra-bot/deploy-bot: observe canary telemetry for 6h, auto-roll back if fallback_rate > 0.5% or perplexity delta > 3%

kevin: thumbs up. I'll drop a tiny script in /tmp/canary-repro and post results.

maria: thanks team. primary hypothesis: L40S allocator fragmentation + unaligned KV tiles -> FP8 kernel partial-tile fallback -> fp16 fallback -> numeric drift. plan is to mitigate via alignment + pre-reserve chunk + session-consistency. will update after scaled run. :hourglass:
